history.prompt: Minimalist modular component assembly on a pale laundry-room shelf, split-screen diptych with left-right scenario contrast. Left half: a wall-mounted smart-home hub with a small mechanical call counter and a short grey ethernet cable; right half: a deck-of-cards brushed-aluminum box with two serial ports, a stubby Bluetooth antenna, a 3.5mm audio jack and a power-over-ethernet socket, resting on a small rubber mat. A washing machine is softly out of focus behind the shelf. One directional key light rakes from the left; palette bone white, graphite, deep pine green. Viewed through a 100mm macro lens, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, no text, no logos.

style_when: the story turns on one physical thing — a part, a material, a component, a document — and what that thing costs, contains or crosses a border is the news
prompt: Split-screen diptych: left half, a macro of a washing machine's recessed network port set in white enamel; right half, an extreme macro of a small matte black home-automation bridge with two serial ports and an Ethernet cable plug held near the socket, both on a painted wood garage shelf. Soft daylight from the left, 100mm macro lens, shallow depth of field, film grain. Slate grey, bone white, graphite. Extreme asymmetry: right-half port sits on the thirds, background falls away.
rationale: The story turns on one physical thing—the port and the $69 box that reaches it—so a macro close-up with shallow depth of field isolates the material reality of the local interface and its cost. The split-screen keeps the cloud-versus-physical contrast explicit without studio abstraction.

core_thesis: A home's running cost now hinges on whether the interface answers locally through a physical port or through a metered cloud account, with SmartThings charging per call and Nabu Casa selling a one-time box for the port.
core_conflict: Cloud-metered API access versus one-time local physical port ownership.
